proof.text: By [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction], $R$ preserves fibrations, trivial fibrations and weak equivalences between fibrant objects. Since a right adjoint preserves the terminal object, $RY$ is fibrant for fibrant $Y$. The composite of the fibration $q_{RY}:QRY\to RY$ with $RY\to *$ is a fibration, so $QRY$ is fibrant and is cofibrant by hypothesis. Closure of fibrations under composition follows directly by solving the two successive lifting problems. Thus the given enriched composite restricts to $F=QR:\mathcal N^{cf}\to\mathcal M^{cf}$. Naturality gives $q_B Qf=fq_A$ for every arrow $f:A\to B$. If $f$ is weak, both $fq_A$ and $q_B$ are weak, so two-out-of-three makes $Qf$ weak. Consequently $F$ preserves weak equivalences between bifibrants. Both bifibrant simplicial categories are locally Kan by applying the simplicial model axiom of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] to the initial map of their source and terminal map of their target.

source.place: Lemma 1.3.4.21, replacement functors; elementary bifibrancy and two-out-of-three argument for the specified Q.

proof.text: Take the coherent derived adjunction $\mathbb L=\mathbf LL\dashv\mathbb R=\mathbf RR$ supplied by [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction], using the underlying ordinary functor $Q$ for cofibrant replacement. For any $X\in\mathcal M$ put $P=QX$, and choose a functorial fibrant replacement $t_{LP}:LP\to TLP$. The map $u_P:P\to RTLP$ adjoint to $t_{LP}$ is weak: $P$ is cofibrant, $TLP$ is fibrant, and $t_{LP}$ is weak, so the assumed Quillen-equivalence criterion applies. The cited derived-unit formula identifies the unit at the localization of $X$ with the localization of $u_P$ after inverting the localization of $q_X$. It is therefore an equivalence. This is the actual coherent unit of the cited adjunction, rather than an independently chosen family of arrows.

source.place: Lemma 1.3.4.21, proof: the map v-prime from a cofibrant object to the right adjoint of a fibrant replacement; application to QX.

proof.text: For fibrant $Y\in\mathcal N$ consider $c_Y:LQRY\xrightarrow{Lq_{RY}}LRY\xrightarrow{\epsilon_Y}Y$. Its ordinary adjoint is $q_{RY}:QRY\to RY$, by naturality of the adjunction bijection and the defining property of $\epsilon$. Since $QRY$ is cofibrant and $Y$ is fibrant, the Quillen-equivalence criterion implies that $c_Y$ is weak. The counit formula of [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] identifies its localization with the derived counit at $Y$. Every object of $\mathcal N_\infty$ is equivalent to a fibrant representative by fibrant replacement, so naturality gives equivalence components everywhere. Step 2 gives the same for the unit. By [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], componentwise equivalences are equivalences in the whole functor quasicategories. Thus these unit and counit transformations exhibit $\mathbb L$ and $\mathbb R$ as coherent inverse equivalences.

source.place: Lemma 1.3.4.21, dual replacement argument for the other composite; actual counit checked using its adjunct, followed by the componentwise criterion.

proof.text: For $\mathcal A=\mathcal M,\mathcal N$, let $B_{\mathcal A}$ be the underlying ordinary category of $\mathcal A^{cf}$, $i_{\mathcal A}:B_{\mathcal A}\to\mathcal A$ its inclusion, and $C_{\mathcal A}=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathcal A^{cf})$. Include the discrete enrichment of $B_{\mathcal A}$ into $\mathcal A^{cf}$ and take coherent nerves, obtaining $j_{\mathcal A}:N(B_{\mathcal A})\to C_{\mathcal A}$. The ordinary-nerve identification of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] says that $j$ sends an ordinary string to the coherent simplex constant at each of its composites. By [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] there is an equivalence $e_{\mathcal A}:C_{\mathcal A}\simeq\mathcal A_\infty$ with $e_{\mathcal A}j_{\mathcal A}\simeq\ell_{\mathcal A}N(i_{\mathcal A})$, where $\ell_{\mathcal A}$ denotes localization. Its statement also says that $N(B_{\mathcal A})[W^{-1}]_\infty\simeq\mathcal A_\infty$ via inclusion. Hence $j_{\mathcal A}$ is itself localization at $W$: compose restriction along $j_{\mathcal A}$ with the equivalence induced by $e_{\mathcal A}$ and use the full functor-category universal property. In particular restriction along $j_{\mathcal A}$ is fully faithful on functor infinity categories.

source.place: Theorem 1.3.4.20, its localization universal property; canonical ordinary-to-coherent nerve map expanded using the subset-poset construction.

proof.text: Put $H=N_{\mathrm{hc}}F$ and let $F_0:B_{\mathcal N}\to B_{\mathcal M}$ be the underlying ordinary functor. The construction in step 4 gives the strict equality $Hj_{\mathcal N}=j_{\mathcal M}N(F_0)$: both sides send a string to the same composites, since $F$ is enriched. Consequently $e_{\mathcal M}Hj_{\mathcal N}\simeq\ell_{\mathcal M}N(QRi_{\mathcal N})$. The ordinary natural transformation $qR:QRi_{\mathcal N}\Rightarrow Ri_{\mathcal N}$ has weak components; after localization its nerve is a coherent natural equivalence by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Thus this last functor is equivalent to $\ell_{\mathcal M}N(Ri_{\mathcal N})$. On the other hand the coherent replacement formula in [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] gives $\mathbb R e_{\mathcal N}j_{\mathcal N}\simeq\ell_{\mathcal M}N(Ri_{\mathcal N})$: every input is fibrant, and the natural comparison $RY\to RTY$ is weak because $R$ preserves weak equivalences between fibrants. This identifies the two precomposed functors, including their transformations, not only their objects.

source.place: Lemma 1.3.4.21 and Remark 1.3.4.27, right derived replacement composite; enriched ordinary-nerve square and qR comparison written explicitly.

proof.text: Restriction along $j_{\mathcal N}$ is fully faithful by step 4. The coherent natural equivalence between the restrictions constructed in step 5 therefore lifts to an equivalence $e_{\mathcal M}H\simeq\mathbb R e_{\mathcal N}$: lift the transformation and its inverse by fullness on mapping spaces, and lift their inverse homotopies by faithfulness. This uses the entire functor-category localization property of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]. Combining it with step 3 and the inverses of $e_{\mathcal M},e_{\mathcal N}$ gives a coherent inverse $K\simeq e_{\mathcal N}^{-1}\mathbb L e_{\mathcal M}$ of $H$, with equivalences $KH\simeq1$ and $HK\simeq1$. Thus the specified $H$, for the given arbitrary enriched $Q$, represents $\mathbf RR$.

source.place: Theorem 1.3.4.20 and Lemma 1.3.4.21; elementary uniqueness through the full localization universal property.

proof.text: The comparison just proved is an equivalence of functors in the functor infinity category. It therefore identifies their actions on mapping spaces and their composition homotopies. More concretely [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] identifies the mapping spaces of $C_{\mathcal A}$ naturally with the actual enriched mapping sets of $\mathcal A^{cf}$, by a comparison preserving enriched composition and its coherent homotopies. Naturality for the simplicial functor $F$ identifies the mapping map induced by $H$ with the given map induced by $QR$, including these composition data. The localization comparison of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] then identifies them with localized derived mapping spaces. The functor equivalence criterion in [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] also shows that these maps are equivalences.

source.place: Theorem 1.3.4.20 with its mapping-space interpretation; explicit use of natural coherent-nerve and localization comparisons.

proof.text: Finally check the stated testing convention for categorical equivalence. For every quasicategory $Z$, precomposition with $H$ gives $H^*:\operatorname{Fun}(C_{\mathcal M},Z)\to\operatorname{Fun}(C_{\mathcal N},Z)$, and precomposition with $K$ is its inverse up to coherent natural equivalence: whisker $KH\simeq1$ and $HK\simeq1$ from step 6 with diagrams into $Z$. These are natural equivalences by the componentwise criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Passing to homotopy categories makes them natural isomorphisms, so $hH^*$ is an equivalence of ordinary categories for every $Z$. This is exactly categorical equivalence in [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. The equivalence unit and counit of the derived adjunction were established in steps 2 and 3. No step asserts that $R$ preserves cofibrant objects.

source.place: Lemma 1.3.4.21, equivalence conclusion interpreted in the Joyal testing convention; elementary whiskering of the displayed inverses.

title: Bifibrant nerve presentation of derived right Quillen equivalences
statement:
Use simplicial model categories, bifibrant objects, the homotopy coherent nerve and infinity localizations of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization], the Quillen derived-adjunction conventions of [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction], and the meaning of combinatorial from [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus]. Let $L:\mathcal M\rightleftarrows\mathcal N:R$ be a simplicial Quillen adjunction between combinatorial simplicial model categories. Assume it is a Quillen equivalence: for each cofibrant $X$ and fibrant $Y$, a map $LX\to Y$ is a weak equivalence if and only if its adjoint $X\to RY$ is a weak equivalence. Work in fixed universes, enlarged to contain the categories and nerves. Let $Q:\mathcal M\to\mathcal M$ be a simplicially enriched functor and $q:Q\Rightarrow\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal M}$ an enriched natural transformation such that every $QX$ is cofibrant and every $q_X:QX\to X$ is a trivial fibration. For any such choice, $QR$ restricts to a simplicial functor $\mathcal N^{cf}\to\mathcal M^{cf}$ and
$$N_{\mathrm{hc}}(QR):N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathcal N^{cf})\longrightarrow N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathcal M^{cf})$$
is a categorical equivalence in the sense of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. Under the localization equivalences of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization], it represents $\mathbf R R$, including its action on mapping spaces and composition homotopies. The derived adjunction $\mathbf L L\dashv\mathbf R R$ has equivalence unit and counit. A trivial fibration means a fibration which is a weak equivalence; no preservation of cofibrant objects by $R$ is assumed.

source.place: Agent-extracted derived-equivalence and specified enriched-replacement presentation from returned item step 7, first two paragraphs. Supporting references: Higher Algebra Theorem 1.3.4.20 and Lemma 1.3.4.21 (localization and Quillen equivalence), read online at https://www.math.ias.edu/~lurie/papers/HA.pdf, printed pp.117-118. No Stacks tag states this enriched comparison theorem; the independent argument is in report.md.
